National Weather Service Burlington VT
242 AM EDT Sat Oct 31 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 225 AM EDT Saturday...

The forecast is in good shape. No major changes needed.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 242 AM EDT Saturday...

1. Dry and cool through Sunday.

2. Increasing warmth early next week with possible light rain 
along the international border.

3. Breezes will be likely ahead of the next precipitation 
chances expected next week. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 242 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Surface high pressure will build into northern New York 
and Vermont throughout the day. It will be a chilly day to wrap up 
the month of October with temperatures lingering in the 40s for most 
locations. Mountain clouds may briefly scatter out, but an upper 
vort will quickly dive southeast and produce some additional mid to 
high clouds mid-afternoon into the evening hours.

Main concern for today will be continued low humidity across the 
region. Eastern slopes of the Adirondacks into south-central Vermont 
will likely observe minimum relative humidities from 30-40%. Areas 
north will likely see values in the 40-50% range. Modest mixing, but 
overall light flow should keep sustained winds around 5-10 mph with 
a few gusts around 15-18 mph during the afternoon.

High pressure will be overhead, and so efficient radiational cooling 
is expected. Trick-or-treaters can expect a chilly experience, but 
at least it will not be the wet and windy weather of last year. 
Temperatures will quickly fall into the 30s after sunset, and 
overnight lows will reach into the 20s for most. During the pre-dawn 
hours, southwesterly flow will become reestablished as high pressure 
moves offshore. Moderating conditions will bring temperatures up 
into the mid 50s to near 60 by Sunday afternoon. Initially low 
dewpoints will begin to rise, and relative humidity will become less 
of a concern. Minimum relative humidity values on Sunday will likely 
be at or above 40% outside a few localized areas in the Upper Valley.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Scanning through the early part of next week, guidance 
continues to trend away from a cold frontal passage Monday night 
into Tuesday. This means warm advection is slated to begin a bit 
sooner. Temperatures will warm into the upper 50s to mid 60s during 
the afternoon, with clouds north. A mid to upper level ridge tilted 
northwest to southeast should let some moisture crest over its axis 
over the eastern Great Lakes region. It's possible some rain will be 
within our side of the international border. Amounts, if any, will 
be light. Even without the rain, there will be greater sky cover. 
This will limit heating a bit for Tuesday, but it will still likely 
climb into the upper 50s to mid 60s during the afternoon.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Models continue to depict a full meridional trough to 
approach late next week. Consensus is moderately strong that ridging 
will slowly slide eastward Tuesday into Wednesday as a large area of 
low pressure is favored to develop over the Plains while jet energy 
is projected to dip into the the southern states. The result could 
be a more mature type front and system passage sometime between 
Wednesday night and Friday night. Passage timing remains most 
suspect given the dependence on the movement speed of a large, semi-
persistent ridge. However, the pressure gradient will likely be 
compounded across the Northeast Wednesday into Thursday supporting 
some southerly breezes and promoting gusts 20-30 mph, especially in 
channeled areas like the northern Champlain Valley. As for 
precipitation, models are split on how exactly the front moves 
through with some supporting a split energy scenario pointing a 
weaker initial wave with potential for an upper low moving in over 
the following weekend. Others remain more consolidated with the wave 
pushing a moderately strong front through the region with an upper 
low dragging behind. Either way, some rain seems probable towards 
the end of next week. Details on "when" and "how much" should become 
clearer over the next few days.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 06Z Sunday...VFR conditions are expected to persist
through the forecast period with flow out of the northwest
generally 5 to 10kts. This direction will promote some potential
for increasing clouds 16-23Z due to upsloping. Could see some 
weak mountain waves continuing as well which are presently 
evident on satellite images. As such, some generally light 
turbulence can be expected in the vicinity of ridge level 
altitudes. Best chances at MVFR CIG will be at SLK, but may not 
consolidate given very dry boundary layer. Winds begin to turn 
more westerly late in the period limiting upslope and ushering 
in more clearing.
